summary: Score per-heater drive responses beyond the drive-linear family (polynomial order 1 and 2, harmonic order 1 and 2 of the returned phase) on job-00, job-01 and the training-only Ascella folds.

reconciliation.note: The families and widths were chosen without a preregistered record; the reading criterion is the one plan ascella-configuration-holdout-training-only fixed before its runs.

next_action: None; constraining these coefficients needs a hardware case that repeats one configuration under perturbed compilations, tracked by plan ascella-signed-coherence-conformance.
scope: Five drive families of the returned 12-mode meshes (shifted Legendre order 1 and 2, harmonic order 1 at tau 0.3 and 0.1, harmonic order 2), each fitted on job-00 from the zero start, scored on job-01 and on the 19 training-only folds that serve the X or Y readout, under the 30-on-10 and below-20 reading.

steps.action: Fit the five families with scripts/ascella_drive_response.py and score every scored configuration's training-only fold with counting plus g C g^T variance.
steps.acceptance: drive-response.json replays within the fit bounds under the gate runner's kernel pair, and each family's X and Y sums carry the reading: 30 or more keeps the shortfall, below 20 with a median variance ratio above 1 is weakly identified.

receipts.result: Polynomial order 1 keeps the X shortfall (32 on 10, variance ratio 10); polynomial order 2 and the three harmonic families fall below 20 with median variance ratios 6.5 to 485 and read as weakly identified. Every family passes job-01 held-out (X 4.0 to 5.4, Y 6.7 to 12.6). The record replays on the merged tree.

resolution: The polynomial order-1 family keeps the left-out X shortfall; the richer families are not identified by 29 training configurations, so the drive-linear section's medium-high confidence stands.

receipts.result: The one step is done; drive-response.json is retained with its replay gate.
